s01_title
This is PakVerify: an AI and blockchain based police verification system, built as our final year project.
s02_problem
Today, a police character certificate means repeated visits to the station, paperwork, and records that are hard to verify. PakVerify moves the whole process online.
s03_auth
Every user signs in with their CNIC, a password and a one-time code, and lands on the dashboard for their role: citizen, police staff, authority, or administrator.
s04_apply
A citizen submits an application and uploads their CNIC and photo.
s05_face
Live face verification follows. ArcFace matches the face with the CNIC photo, and a head-turn challenge rejects printed photos and screens.
s06_review
The criminal-record check runs automatically. Staff review the documents, and the authority approves the case.
s07_cert
After online payment, the certificate is issued with a QR code.
s08_chat_citizen
Each role also gets its own assistant. A citizen can track only their own application, and is refused when they ask for a criminal-record lookup.
s09_chat_police
Police staff can search the local criminal-record dataset by CNIC, and an administrator can check certificates within their province.
s10_admin
The administrator dashboard brings together applications, staff accounts, analytics and audit logs.
s11_chain
Key actions are written to a SHA-256 hash-chain ledger. The blockchain explorer shows every block, and the full history of any application.
s12_integrity
To check a certificate, an officer uploads the PDF. The original matches its stored hash. Change a single name, and the hash no longer matches, so it is flagged as tampered.
s13_qr
Anyone can also scan the QR code to see the certificate's status, its hash, and its record on the Ethereum Sepolia test network.
s14_tech
PakVerify is built with React, Django REST and PostgreSQL, ArcFace face matching on ONNX Runtime, and a Solidity smart contract on Sepolia.
s15_end
Faster, transparent, and tamper-proof police verification. Thank you.
